title: Global OT Application Engineer
description:
The Global OT Application Engineer implements, integrates, tests, deploys and supports industrial applications across manufacturing sites. The role configures and implements global use cases and applications.


The Application Engineer is the technical bridge between plants, application owners, developers, infrastructure and cybersecurity teams, software vendors and system integrators. The role covers both purchased or configured applications and internally built solutions; it is neither limited to software development nor to coordination.

**Assigned scope:**

* Global OT applications across manufacturing sites, including MES/MOM, SCADA, IIoT and CMMS domains.
* Purchased, configured and internally developed applications and their interfaces to plant and business systems.

**Primary emphasis:**

* Applications are deployed safely, consistently and with clear acceptance evidence.
* Plant systems exchange accurate and reliable data through governed interfaces.
* Sites receive effective onboarding, technical support and operational handover.
* Incidents and recurring technical problems are resolved at the appropriate support level.
* Global templates and standards are applied without losing control of necessary local adaptations.

**Main tasks / Standard of performance**

**Implementation and Integration:**

* Configure and implement applications, templates and technical components in accordance with the approved solution design.
* Gather requirements to integrate applications with PLC, SCADA, DCS, MES/MOM, IIoT, historians and business systems such as ERP, LIMS or QMS.
* Configure and troubleshoot industrial data exchange using technologies such as OPC UA, MQTT, REST APIs and SQL.
* Ensure that global libraries, naming conventions, templates, interfaces and deployment standards are followed.
* Document any approved local deviation from the global template, including its justification and approval, in the application documentation.
* Review technical and functional deliveries from developers, vendors and system integrators and challenge gaps in quality, maintainability or operability.

**Testing and Validation:**

* Translate approved requirements and designs into a complete and traceable technical test scope.
* Prepare and execute functional, integration and regression tests and support FAT, SAT and user acceptance testing.
* Diagnose bugs, coordinate correction and test cycles, and maintain clear test evidence and release documentation.
* Verify connectivity, data integrity, performance, resilience, security controls and operational readiness.
* Confirm that acceptance criteria are met before recommending release or production deployment.

**Deployment and Site Onboarding:**

* Lead the technical work required to take an application from a controlled release into stable plant operation.
* Assess site readiness, infrastructure, signals, interfaces, data availability and local dependencies.
* Coordinate technical activities with plant stakeholders, local OT teams, vendors and system integrators.
* Execute or supervise installation, configuration, commissioning and cut\-over activities.
* Provide hypercare, technical training, documentation and a clear handover to support and site teams.

**Operations and Support:**

* Provide ITIL\-based L2/L3 application support: advanced troubleshooting, functional bug\-fixing and technical incident escalation across sites (ITIL support levels, not Purdue Model network layers).
* Perform problem management: conduct root\-cause analysis (RCA) and implement corrective and preventive actions (CAPA) for recurring application errors.
* Manage technical change requests: oversee software modifications from assessment through testing, release and production deployment.
* Monitor application health: track application performance, data interfaces (APIs) and support trends to recommend continuous improvements.
* Maintain knowledge databases: manage technical documentation, application runbooks, release notes and Known\-Error Databases (KEDB).

**Plant and Technical Team Interface:**

* Act as the practical interface between plant operations and the teams that design, build and supply the applications.
* Translate plant constraints and operational issues into actionable technical requirements and bugs.
* Explain technical options, dependencies, risks and decisions to plant and business stakeholders.
* Coordinate effectively with the Application Owner on priorities, scope, standards and acceptance.
* Work with developers on build activities and with delivery leads or Scrum Masters on planning and execution.
* Challenge vendors and system integrators on technical quality, delivery evidence and issue resolution, escalating commercial or roadmap matters to the Application Owner.

**Skills and competencies**

**Functional \& Technical Competencies:**

* Strong knowledge of at least one relevant application domain: MES/MOM, SCADA, IIoT or CMMS, and of interfaces to PLC, SCADA and DCS systems.
* Practical integration knowledge using OPC UA, MQTT, REST APIs and SQL.
* Ability to read, adapt or create components using Python, C\#, Java or JavaScript when needed.
* Working knowledge of versioning, release, incident, problem and change\-management practices.
* Working knowledge of ISA\-95 principles, OT cybersecurity and regulated validation requirements where applicable.

**Behavioral Competencies:**

* Plant\-oriented, pragmatic and structured, with strong ownership of technical issues.
* Constructive challenge of delivery evidence from developers, vendors and system integrators.
* Clear cross\-functional communication across plant, specialist and external audiences.

**Experience**

**Minimum Qualifications:**

* Bachelor's or master's degree in automation, electrical, software or industrial engineering, or comparable practical experience.
* Experience with industrial applications, automation, MES/MOM, SCADA, IIoT or comparable manufacturing systems; senior appointments normally require demonstrated responsibility across multiple sites or complex industrial programs.
* Professional English; additional languages relevant to the assigned region are an advantage.

**Working Conditions and Location:**

* Primary European hiring locations Barcelona and southern or western Germany, plus a senior regional position in the north\-eastern United States.
* Home\-based or hybrid working with regular domestic and international travel to manufacturing sites.

**Responsibility / Power of authority**

**The Application Engineer:**

* Together with the Project Managers, defines implementation and configuration approaches within approved standards.
* Stops or rejects a technical deployment when readiness or acceptance criteria are not met.
* Recommends fixes, improvements and standard changes based on operational evidence.
* Escalates architecture, security, scope and vendor\-performance risks.
* The role does not own application strategy, roadmap, backlog or commercial vendor decisions, does not act only as a software developer without integration, testing, support and site responsibilities, does not replace the plant's operational ownership or bypass agreed OT governance, and does not approve material deviations from global standards without the relevant owner or authority.

**Team work / Team membership**

**Communicates to:**

* Application Owner: priorities, scope, standards, acceptance and escalation of commercial or roadmap matters.
* Plant operations and local OT teams: site readiness, deployment activities, onboarding, training, support and operational handover.
* Developers, delivery leads and Scrum Masters: build activities, defect resolution, planning and release execution.
* Infrastructure and cybersecurity teams: interfaces, security controls, architecture dependencies and technical risk.
* Software vendors and system integrators: technical quality, delivery evidence, testing and issue resolution.
* Business and functional stakeholders (production, quality, maintenance, supply chain): technical options, dependencies, risks and decisions affecting plant operations.
* Project managers: rollout planning and execution; sequencing, dependencies and escalation of deviations.

title: Product Owner - Mainloop
location: Sant Cugat del Vallès, CT, ES
description:
**Product Owner**
=================


Own the product, not the ticket queue — the business relationship, the backlog, acceptance, and whether the thing actually gets used.


Mainloop is a **new engineering team inside an established international group**. We are in Barcelona, we are being built from scratch this year, and we have the backing, the customers and the product portfolio of a company that has been around for decades. You get the interesting part of a new team without the part where you check whether payroll clears.


Two more things about where this comes from and where it goes. **The group has been running a techlab in Casablanca for more than eight years** — Barcelona is its second, built to sit closer to the teams we build for, and AI\-native from the first commit, because it starts from a blank page. And the plan does not stop at internal work: **within about a year and a half we intend to externalise** — external clients, our products sold on the market, products developed for it. The first eighteen months are deliberately spent building as much as possible for the group while the machine gets set up. You would arrive at the start of that curve, not after it.


What we build is the software that automates professional\-services work — across roughly fifteen countries, for businesses drowning in administration: the forms, the approvals, the reconciliations, the spreadsheet somebody rebuilds every month. We work in two halves. One half goes into a business, finds out what really happens there, and proves fast whether an idea is worth having. **The other half — your half — takes what is proven and owns it for years: gathers the needs, keeps building, gets it adopted, and makes sure it stays worth having.** Most automation teams stop at the demo. The entire point of ours is that we do not.

**We are not looking for a backlog administrator.** If your last role was turning other people's decisions into tickets and running the ceremonies around them, this is a different job. Here you are the product manager *and* the product owner: there is no one above you writing the strategy for your products, and no one below you writing the stories. What should exist, in what order, and whether what shipped is right — that is yours.

##### **What the job actually is**


A product arrives with a handover pack — already proven with its stakeholders by the first half of the team, already hardened for production. From day one it belongs to you and one developer, as a pair, for its life.

* **You own the relationship with the business.** Real people, in real offices, whose working day your product either improves or does not. You go and sit with them. Not a ticket queue — trust, built in person, held over years.
* **You gather the needs and you decide.** Your users cannot churn — they are in the building, and they will bring you more requests than any team could build. Most of this job is choosing: what moves the outcome, what waits, and what you decline with a reason the person asking can respect. **Saying no well is the defining skill here**, and you will have a product vision to say it from.
* **You write what should exist, precisely.** In our team, coding agents build most of what ships, steered by your developer. Agents amplify whatever they are given: a sharp specification becomes working software astonishingly fast, and a vague one becomes a thousand lines of confidently wrong code. Your needs, rules, edge cases and acceptance criteria are the most load\-bearing documents in the company. Writing them precisely is the highest\-leverage hour of your week.
* **You accept, or you don't.** When something ships, you are the person who checks the behaviour against what you wrote — with your own hands, in the product, against the criteria you set before the build. "The demo looked right" is not acceptance. You will get seriously good at defining what "done right" means in a way that can actually be checked.
* **You get it adopted, and you measure.** Our products do not have revenue to hide behind. A product that ships and is not used is a failure with good release notes. You own the follow\-up, the onboarding of new users with the business, and the number that says whether the thing is working — time saved, error rate, uptake — and you report that number whether it flatters us or not.
* **You carry a portfolio, not a product.** Every product we own is built on the same scaffold and arrives the same shape, which is what makes it possible for one PO to run several — each with its own developer, each with its own business. Variety is structural here: new products keep arriving from the other half of the team.
* **Your first product is real.** A live platform that a business runs on every day — real users, real history, real stakes. You inherit it from the person who has been carrying it, and part of your first months is taken up with the most useful thing a new PO can do: learning it properly before changing it.

##### **Why this job exists — the honest version**


Here is the thing our industry has just learned, and it is the reason we are hiring you: **AI made building fast, and it did not make building the right thing any more likely.** Surveys now find most companies shipping faster with AI while almost none can point to the return. It has never been easier to run, at speed, in the wrong direction.


In a team like ours the engineers steer agents, and implementation is rarely the bottleneck. **The bottleneck is deciding** — what to build, for whom, in what order, and whether what shipped actually did what the business needed. That is not a job the agents do. It is not really a job most engineers want. It is *this* job, and in an AI\-native team it is a more senior, more consequential job than the same title has ever been — because every decision you write down gets built, quickly, exactly as you wrote it.

**What stays yours, permanently:**

* **Deciding what not to build.** The agents will cheerfully build anything. Somebody has to be the person for whom "no" is a complete sentence with a number attached.
* **The relationship.** Being trusted by a business, reading what they need underneath what they ask for, and telling them a favourite idea is not worth it — there is no model for that.
* **Precision about what should exist.** Turning a messy, human, political need into a specification with exactly one correct interpretation is the hardest writing there is, and it is now the closest thing this industry has to source code.
* **Judgement about what came back.** Acceptance, in a world where software appears fast, is the quality bar. You are it.
* **The outcome.** Whether the business is actually better off. Somebody has to own that number rather than the ship date, and it is you.

##### **You will define how the PO role works here**


You are the first. That is not a gap in the org chart — it is the offer.


How product ownership works in an AI\-native team is a genuinely open question in our industry right now, and the honest answer is that nobody's playbook fits yet. Ours will be written here, over your first year, by you and Edouard together: how needs become specs, how acceptance works when agents build, how adoption gets measured, how many products one pair can carry. The POs we hire after you will be onboarded onto the way you built.


If you have ever read a process document and thought *I could have written this better* — this is the job where you get to.

##### **You will get seriously good at building with AI**


We are an AI\-native team, genuinely — not a team that added a Copilot licence. Everyone gets their own Claude Max subscription and the tooling to use it properly, and that includes you. The product people we admire in this market prototype with AI before they ask anyone to build: a rough working version of an idea, made in an afternoon, shown to a stakeholder — because a prototype communicates intent better than any document, and because it kills bad ideas cheaply. You will learn to do that here if you cannot already, and you will learn what makes a specification one an agent builds correctly the first time. That skill is being repriced upward across our entire industry, and this is one of very few jobs where you would practise it daily on products people depend on.

##### **The Mainloop Barcelona certificate**


Something we are building alongside the team, and we think it is genuinely unusual.


Over your first two to three years here you work through a defined body of knowledge — how we build, how we run products, how a need becomes a spec becomes working, adopted software — and when you can demonstrably run a product our way, you are awarded the **Mainloop Barcelona certificate**. It is yours: it goes on your CV, and we intend to make it mean something in this market. For a product person specifically, it certifies the thing the market is newly desperate for — that you can own products in an AI\-native team, end to end, with proof.

##### **How we build**

**Every product starts from the same scaffold, and it is the same in most of our repos — deliberately.** For you that is the whole point: every product in your portfolio has the same shape, so carrying several does not mean holding several different worlds in your head. It also means the handover pack you inherit from the first half of the team actually tells you how the thing works — because it is built the way everything else is built.


You do not need to arrive knowing our tooling, and this ad deliberately lists no technologies. You need to be technical enough to hold your own in an engineering discussion, and to read what an agent produced closely enough to judge it. The rest — our architecture, our patterns, our method — is what we train you on.

##### **Things worth knowing up front**

* **Barcelona is your base, and you will spend real time with the businesses.** The products serve people across roughly fifteen countries, and the relationship is the job — expect regular travel to sit with your users, on us. It is a fraction of what our deployed engineers do, but it is not zero, and the POs who never leave the office are the ones whose products stop being used.
* **Nobody is on call. Ever.** No rota, no pager. Alerts post to a channel and wait for morning. We protect evenings with engineering, not with people.
* **Nobody counts your hours or your tickets.** What gets looked at is whether your products are used, whether the business is better off, and whether your specs held up. Outcomes, not throughput.
* **We are building the team this year, and you will shape how it works.** That is truest of all for this seat — see above.

##### **If you would be moving to Barcelona for this**

**We do not expect you to absorb the cost of relocating, and we would rather say what we cover than leave you to ask.**

* **We pay to get you here.** Flights, your first month's accommodation while you find somewhere of your own, the visa and paperwork costs, and **an agent to handle the bureaucracy** — the NIE, the TIE appointment, the apostilles — instead of leaving you to meet the Spanish administrative system alone. Spanish lessons if you want them — and in this seat they will pay for themselves.
* **A relocation bonus, paid on arrival rather than dripped out.** It is repayable only if you leave within the first eighteen months, and that condition is the reason we can pay it up front — moving countries costs money at the start, not in year two.

**Three things here are worth more than they look on an offer comparison, particularly against a US one:**

* **Healthcare with no premium, no deductible and no network** — from day one, and not tied to staying in this job.
* **Thirty calendar days of holiday — that is 22 working days — plus fourteen public holidays**, roughly seven weeks in total. That is the statutory floor in Spain, not a benefit we are being generous with.
* **Nobody is on call. Ever.** It has its own line above and we mean it literally.

**If you are coming from the United States**, two things are usually worth more than the headline salary gap and almost nobody has done the arithmetic: **a salary here can sit below the Foreign Earned Income Exclusion**, and **federal student loans on an income\-driven plan are assessed on the income that exclusion has already removed.** We are not your tax advisor and you should get one — but ask in the first conversation and we will walk you through the comparison we ran, including the parts where the number comes out smaller.

##### **What we are looking for**

**One bar sits above everything else, so here it is plainly.** You can own a product end to end — the need, the decision, the specification, the acceptance, the outcome — and you are **technical enough to contribute to an engineering discussion and to judge what an AI agent built.** You do not need to code for a living. You do need to have no fear of the inside of the machine. If you read that and thought *that is the job I want*, keep reading.

**Read the rest as a description of the person you will be here, not a checklist you have to arrive with.** Almost nobody ticks all of it on day one, and we would rather hire the judgement and train the rest.

* **You have owned something real.** A product, a platform, a module — something in production, with users, where the backlog, the priorities and the outcome were genuinely yours. We will ask you to walk us through it, and to justify specific decisions inside it.
* **You are interested in how businesses actually work.** Processes, the mess in them, and why people do the odd things they do. Our products automate administrative work, and the PO who finds that boring will be bored.
* **You write with precision, and you like it.** The spec, the acceptance criteria and the "no, because…" are all documents, all read by people (and agents) who were not in the room. If your writing is where your thinking happens, you will be at home.
* **You can say no to someone senior, with a number.** And keep the relationship.
* **You use AI seriously** — for prototyping, for analysis, for your own writing — and you read what it produces the way you would read a colleague's work: with respect and suspicion.
* **You are comfortable with engineers**, and they with you. Our model is one PO and one developer owning each product together. That pair only works if you feed each other context instead of passing tickets over a wall.
* **English, fluently.** It is our working language — we work across roughly fifteen countries. Spanish is a genuine advantage day to day, and for your first product especially. Catalan is not required.
* **Barcelona**, with travel to your businesses.

**We do not care what you studied, and a Scrum certification is neither required nor an advantage.** We care what you have owned, what happened to it, and whether you can talk us through the decisions in it.

##### **How we hire**


Our process is unusual, so here it is up front. Four rounds, and none of them is a puzzle.

* **Fifteen minutes with Edouard.** A short first conversation — who you are, what you are after, and what this actually is. Enough for both of us to work out whether the next one is worth an hour.
* **A thirty\-minute conversation.** What you have owned, how you work, and how you think about it. We will ask you to walk us through a product you owned, and then to justify one specific prioritisation decision inside it: why that, why then, what you declined to do instead. There is no way to prepare for that and it is not meant to catch you out; it is how we tell ownership from proximity.
* **A conversation with our Casablanca team.** The group has run a tech lab there for more than eight years. You get people who have run production at real scale asking their own questions — and you get to ask them yours, including the ones you would rather not ask the person hiring you.
* **A working session built around a real product.** You read a real handover pack, sit with a real stakeholder, decide what matters, write the specification and the acceptance criteria — and then watch what our agents and your developer counterpart build from it, and tell us whether you would accept it, and what it would be worth. It is the closest thing to the real job we could design, and it works both ways: you will know a great deal about whether you want to work here by the end of it.

Our Oncology strategy is built with one goal in mind – pushing the boundaries of science to deliver life\-changing medicines to patients. We have a passion for discovery and a broad pipeline of next\-generation medicines, and together with a focus on execution excellence, we aim to expand treatment options and improve outcomes for patients with solid and haematological cancers. With multiple indications and high\-quality molecules at all stages of our innovative pipeline, we keep pushing forward. Focusing on cutting\-edge science with the latest technology to achieve breakthroughs. 1\) **Clinical Study Assignment:** You will join a clinical study team and build experience as a medical leader in clinical development which could be in Early Clinical Development, Late Clinical Development, or one year in each. * Establishing and approving scientific methods for design and implementation of applicable clinical protocols, data collection systems, and final reports

2\) **Rotational program:** During the course of your program, you will be involved in 3\-6 month long rotations across various groups to gain a better understanding of the cross\-functional departments. This could include:


* Patient safety
* Clinical operations
* Regulatory affairs
* Biostatistics

You will be able to harness rich internal datasets and expertise, aiming to deliver a research project at the end of the Program which will be presented to key internal stakeholders, at a key scientific meeting and published in a peer\-reviewed journal.

We optimize for productivity and performance, not time spent in an office. Help us build an optimal work environment that fits you as an individual.

title: Controller Financiero
description:
AL1 busca para empresa Internacional del sector farma en etapa de expansión con alto nivel de crecimiento sostenido, un **Group Financial Reporting \& Compliance Specialist.**

Se unirá al equipo financiero internacional en plena expansión y ocupará un puesto de nueva creación donde dará forma y desarrollará la función de Cumplimiento e Información Financiera del Grupo.

Reportando directamente al Director Financiero (CFO), desempeñará un papel clave en el fortalecimiento de la gobernanza financiera de las operaciones internacionales (4 sedes, incluida España) y colaborará con un equipo financiero de gran experiencia. Durante el primer año, recibirá mentoría estructurada y asumirá progresivamente la responsabilidad de proyectos estratégicos.

Es una excelente oportunidad para un profesional de las finanzas ambicioso que busque impulsar su carrera hacia un puesto directivo o de alto nivel.

**Funciones principales**

Información financiera del Grupo

* Coordinar la preparación de los estados financieros legales (estatutarios) del Grupo y sus filiales.
* Apoyar el proceso anual de consolidación del Grupo y la elaboración de informes trimestrales para el Consejo de Administración.
* Garantizar el cumplimiento puntual de las obligaciones de presentación de información financiera legal en las distintas jurisdicciones.

Cumplimiento fiscal del Grupo

* Coordinar el cumplimiento fiscal periódico del Grupo (impuesto de sociedades, IVA, IRPF, declaraciones informativas).
* Apoyar el proceso de cierre fiscal anual y la documentación de precios de transferencia.
* Aplicar las directrices del BOICAC/ICAC y gestionar la respuesta a inspecciones fiscales.
* Gestionar los beneficios fiscales por I\+D (Art. 35 LIS) y los informes justificativos correspondientes.
* Coordinar la presupuestación, el seguimiento y la justificación de subvenciones para proyectos de I\+D financiados con fondos públicos.
* Actuar como enlace con organismos como CDTI, MICIU, AEAT y auditores externos.
* Apoyar la solicitud de programas de financiación nacionales y europeos (CDTI, Horizon Europe, PERTE, CIEN, NEOTEC).

CAPEX, activos intangibles y partidas del balance

* Gestionar la capitalización de activos fijos y amortizaciones (transición desde el área de Tesorería prevista para 2026\).
* Documentar y preparar la justificación de activos intangibles (especialmente en I\+D).
* Negociar rappels comerciales y revisar las pólizas de seguro de la empresa.

Auditoría externa y control interno

* Coordinar las auditorías anuales con auditores externos en las distintas jurisdicciones.
* Desarrollar y fortalecer los procedimientos de control interno y la matriz de controles (segregación de funciones/SoD, conciliaciones, autorizaciones).

Mejora de procedimientos y políticas

* Revisar los procedimientos en las distintas sedes y proponer mejoras.
* Mantener actualizadas las políticas contables y la documentación de NetSuite.
* Cumplimentar encuestas oficiales (INE, Banco de España) y atender los requisitos normativos.

Se ofrece

* Salario más bonificación.
* Horario flexible.
* Modalidad de trabajo híbrida (6 días al mes).
* 23 días de vacaciones anuales.
* Desarrollo profesional totalmente financiado, incluyendo formación técnica, certificaciones y cursos de idiomas.
* Mentoría directa por parte del CFO durante el primer año.
* Clara proyección de carrera hacia puestos de liderazgo financiero de alto nivel.
* Exposición a operaciones internacionales en diversas jurisdicciones europeas.
* Oportunidad de construir y dar forma a un área financiera de nueva creación.
* Entorno de trabajo colaborativo, internacional e impulsado por la innovación.

**Requisitos**

Formación

* Grado en Contabilidad, Finanzas, Administración de Empresas, Economía o afín.
* Se valorará Máster en Auditoría, Fiscalidad, Finanzas o Cumplimiento Normativo (Compliance).
* Se valorarán certificaciones profesionales como ACCA, ROAC (en curso), CIA o similares.

Experiencia

* 3 a 5 años de experiencia en auditoría externa y/o contabilidad corporativa.
* Experiencia en la preparación de estados financieros legales/estatutarios.
* Experiencia en el apoyo a auditorías externas.
* Conocimiento de la normativa contable y fiscal española.
* Se valorará muy positivamente la experiencia en entornos multinacionales.
* La experiencia en precios de transferencia o subvenciones de I\+D será una ventaja, aunque no es imprescindible; ofrecemos apoyo para el aprendizaje en estas áreas.
* Idiomas: Español fluido / Inglés a nivel profesional (C1 o superior). Se valorará el conocimiento de alemán o italiano, aunque no es obligatorio.

title: Customer Complaints Senior Manager
description:
**Who We Are**
At OKX, we believe that the future will be reshaped by crypto, and ultimately contribute to every individual's freedom. OKX is a leading crypto exchange, and the developer of OKX Wallet, giving millions access to crypto trading and decentralized crypto applications (dApps). OKX is also a trusted brand by hundreds of large institutions seeking access to crypto markets. We are safe and reliable, backed by our Proof of Reserves. Across our multiple offices globally, we are united by our core principles: We Before Me, Do the Right Thing, and Get Things Done. These shared values drive our culture, shape our processes, and foster a friendly, rewarding, and diverse environment for every OK\-er. OKX is part of OKG, a group that brings the value of Blockchain to users around the world, through our leading products OKX, OKX Wallet, OKLink and more.

**About the Opportunity**
The Compliance function at OKX is responsible for the overall compliance culture at the company. We're a team of risk\-minded problem solvers who advise the business on the company's regulatory obligations and enterprise risk.
In this role, you will own OKX's Global Customer Complaints Program and report directly to the Compliance Chief of Staff. You will work closely with Local Compliance, Legal, Customer Support, Product, Operations, and Risk teams to promote consistent complaint handling across jurisdictions, maintain alignment with regulatory requirements, and provide effective second\-line oversight and challenge.
A key part of the role will be turning customer complaints into actionable compliance and conduct\-risk intelligence. You will oversee complaints governance and quality assurance, identify trends and potential systemic issues, support root\-cause analysis and remediation, and provide senior leadership with clear reporting on customer outcomes and emerging risks.
You will also support the development, coordination, and tracking of responses to regulators, working directly with Legal and Local Compliance teams on regulatory inquiries, escalated complaints, and related supervisory matters. This requires strong regulatory judgment, excellent written communication, and the ability to coordinate complex matters across multiple teams and jurisdictions.

**What You'll Be Doing**
* Develop, coordinate, and track responses to regulatory inquiries, examinations, and escalated complaints, partnering with Legal and Local Compliance teams to gather and validate facts, prepare clear and defensible responses, manage review and approval processes, meet regulatory deadlines, and track resulting commitments, remediation, and follow\-up through closure.
* Maintain global regulatory alignment by partnering with local Heads of Compliance to identify changes in jurisdictional requirements and ensure global policies, standards, procedures, and local requirements remain current and appropriately implemented.
* Oversee the end\-to\-end complaints control framework, including complaint identification and classification, regulatory and internal service\-level requirements, escalation thresholds, documentation standards, investigation and resolution expectations, and closed\-loop validation.
* Own the second\-line oversight and quality assurance, including risk\-based testing of complaint handling, identification of control gaps and customer\-outcome issues, tracking of remediation, and escalation of issues.
* Turn complaint data into actionable compliance and conduct\-risk intelligence by monitoring trends, recurring issues, root causes, regulatory complaints, overdue cases, customer outcomes, and potential systemic issues requiring broader investigation or remediation.
* Own complaints governance and executive reporting, including reporting to compliance committees and serving as the standing owner of the complaints agenda for compliance leadership meetings.
* Maintain the complaint management database, service level agreement adherence, and escalation thresholds across all regions.
* Serve as the central Compliance point of contact for material complaint matters, including complaints or inquiries escalated to regulators, ensuring consistent governance, appropriate escalation, and defensible documentation.
* Drive continuous improvement of the framework, using QA results, regulatory developments, complaint trends, and lessons learned to strengthen controls and improve customer outcomes globally.

**What We Look For In You**

title: Director, UX Design - AEC Forma Design

description:
**About Us**


HarZa is a fast\-growing operator of direct\-to\-consumer brands in health and wellness. Our flagship brand, Rejuvacare, serves over 400,000 customers who trust us with their health, and we are now launching and scaling new portfolio brands. The company has scaled 12x in a single year to over 150 people across 15\+ countries. We are remote\-first, async\-first, and hold a high standard of accountability across everything we do. Paid media is our growth engine, and creative volume is what makes it scale.

**The Role**


You will be the editing engine of a performance pod: a small team built around a creative strategist, a media buyer, and a copywriter, shipping direct\-response ads for claims\-led health and wellness brands. This is not a brand content role and not an organic social role. Every asset you cut exists to convert on paid traffic, and your work is measured by how it performs, not only by how it looks.


The creative challenge is specific: our products solve problems (chronic pain, mobility, wellbeing) whose results are not visually obvious. Your edits build belief through mechanism explanation, testimonials, UGC structures, advertorials, and VSL\-style long form, always with awareness that we operate in a compliance\-sensitive category. You will produce both short\-form ads (15 to 60 seconds) and long\-form direct\-response formats (2 to 6 minutes), and a large part of your week is iterating winners: new hooks, new openings, cutdowns, and format variations of ads that are already scaling.


This is a high\-volume seat and we say so openly. The target output is at least one long\-form ad of around 5 minutes plus 2 to 3 short\-form videos per working day, which comes to roughly 15 to 20 delivered assets per week including iterations. If that rhythm sounds extreme, this is not the right role. If it sounds like the environment you already work in, we should talk.

**What You Will Own**


Direct\-response editing at volume. Editing short\-form and long\-form paid ads from strategist scripts and briefs, shipping platform\-native formats for Meta, TikTok, and YouTube, and sustaining the daily delivery target of one long\-form plus 2 to 3 short\-form videos without sacrificing the craft details that drive performance: hooks, pacing, captions, sound design, and pattern interrupts.


Winner iteration and creative testing. Producing hook variations, cutdowns, re\-orders, and format swaps of winning ads as a first\-class deliverable. Feeding the testing loop the pod runs every week and turning performance feedback into the next round of edits quickly.


Claims\-led storytelling. Building belief for outcomes the viewer cannot see: visualizing mechanisms, structuring testimonial and UGC narratives, editing advertorial and VSL long form that holds attention for minutes, and handling claims with compliance awareness.


Pod collaboration and documentation. Working async\-first inside the pod with your strategist and media buyer, keeping Asana as the single source of truth for briefs, versions, and delivery status, and turning feedback into revised cuts without friction or ego.

 **Requirements**  

Proven experience editing paid direct\-response ads for DTC or ecommerce brands, where your videos ran on real media budgets and you saw the numbers. Fluency in both short\-form ad formats and long\-form DR (VSLs, advertorials, 2\+ minute belief\-building videos). A demonstrated high\-volume rhythm: you have sustained daily ad output in a testing environment, not one polished piece per week. Working knowledge of the metrics that judge your work (hook rate, hold rate, CTR, CPA or ROAS) and a track record of letting data change your edits. Experience in health, wellness, supplements, or other claims\-sensitive verticals is a strong plus. Full professional proficiency with a modern editing stack, reliable remote setup, and the self\-management to thrive in an async\-first, output\-measured company.

 **Benefits**  

A fully remote position at a high\-growth DTC operator launching new brands. Real ownership inside a performance pod where your work directly drives scale. Paid time off, wellness stipend, company\-funded computer allowance after tenure milestone, monthly bonus structure, birthday gift card, and in\-country meetup allowance. A culture that rewards output, speed, and mastery of craft.

title: Senior Direct Response Funnel Copywriter & Strategist
description:
About Us


HarZa Group is a fast\-growing operator of direct\-to\-consumer brands in health and wellness. Our flagship brand, Rejuvacare, serves more than 400,000 customers with products targeting chronic pain and mobility, including RejuvaKnee, FootRenew, RejuvaFlow and OzemPatch. We ship primarily to the United States and run a membership program that powers recurring revenue. The company has scaled 12x in a single year to nearly 150 people across more than 15 countries. We are remote\-first, async\-first, and hold a high standard of accountability across everything we do.


The Role


We are looking for an exceptional senior direct response copywriter to take ownership of our post\-click funnels. This is not a role for someone who receives a brief, writes the copy and moves on. We are looking for someone who treats funnels the way an exceptional creative strategist treats advertising: research the customer and the market, form a hypothesis, develop the concept, write the copy, get the funnel launched, study the performance, identify the constraint, develop the next test, and turn every result into a feedback loop.


You will be deeply involved in the commercial performance of everything you write. Once a funnel goes live you should be watching click\-through rates, advertorial to sales page click\-through, quiz completion, sales page and checkout conversion, revenue per visitor, average order value, order bump and upsell take rates, refund rates and contribution margin. A page is not finished when the copy is approved. It is finished when it has launched, been measured, and produced a learning that improves the next page.


Your ultimate objective is to remove the founders from writing and reviewing routine funnel copy. Initially they will remain closely involved and may still write a large share of it. You will work directly with them, learn their frameworks, understand their decision\-making, and gradually take ownership of the function. Success means reaching the point where the founders no longer need to write funnel copy, rewrite your work, or independently double\-check it before launch. From there you create leverage through AI systems, documented processes and, in time, additional writers trained and managed beneath you.


A Note on the Category


This is claims\-led direct response, not product\-led ecommerce, and the distinction matters more than any other line in this description. Our products address chronic pain and mobility. The benefit is not visually obvious, it cannot be demonstrated in a photograph, and it cannot be sold on aspiration. Belief has to be built through mechanism, proof, advertorial and presell structure, and honest handling of objections, all inside the compliance limits of a health category.


Copywriters who have scaled fashion, accessories, beauty or other visually self\-evident products often find that their playbook does not transfer. A strong track record in a product\-led category is welcome but does not substitute for this. We will prioritize candidates who have written for health, wellness, supplements or another claims\-sensitive category and who understand what can and cannot be said.


Why This Role Is Different


The founders have generated more than nine figures in post\-purchase upsell revenue in under twenty\-four months. That figure is post\-purchase upsell revenue specifically, not total front\-end company revenue. You will get direct access to the frameworks behind those results, existing research, templates, processes and funnel data, direct feedback and training from the founders, a portfolio of brands and offers with significant traffic, a high\-volume testing environment where your ideas get launched and measured, and real commercial data across multiple funnel types, offers and traffic sources.


This is an opportunity to develop beyond being a copywriter. The right person can progress toward Head of Funnel Copy, Head of Funnel Strategy, Director of Conversion, or operator of one of our portfolio brands. We prefer to promote from within, and progression is based on commercial results, leadership ability and the amount of responsibility you can absorb.

 **Requirements**  

What You Will Own


Post\-Click Funnel Strategy


Act as the strategic owner of post\-click messaging and conversion copy. Participate in marketing, campaign and offer planning, understand what each traffic source needs after the click, and ensure message continuity between the advertisement, presell page, sales page, checkout and upsell journey. Recommend the right funnel format based on the offer, traffic source, customer awareness and market sophistication, and determine when a campaign needs an advertorial, listicle, quiz, long\-form page, short\-form page or another structure. Collaborate with media buyers and creative strategists to understand the promise that generated the click, and identify disconnects between the ad message and the landing page experience. Your remit begins at the click, but you must understand the whole acquisition system to make intelligent post\-click decisions.


Customer and Market Research


Research the customer before developing the copy. Analyze reviews, surveys, support tickets, customer interviews, call transcripts, refund reasons and community discussions. Study competitor offers, positioning, mechanisms, pricing and funnel structures. Identify desires, fears, frustrations, failed solutions, objections and buying triggers, understand the customer's level of awareness and the sophistication of the market, and distinguish between what customers say they want and what their behaviour suggests they value. Build voice\-of\-customer libraries that preserve the language customers actually use, validate that claims are supportable and appropriate for the category, and convert raw research into usable copy insight rather than research documents nobody reads.


Hypothesis Before Writing


Every meaningful funnel project begins with a clear hypothesis. Identify the metric or funnel stage being targeted, diagnose the likely reason for underperformance, state the customer insight behind the diagnosis, define what will change and why it should influence behaviour, select a primary success metric and the guardrails around it, and determine what result would validate or invalidate the idea. The first question is not what copy should I write. It is what is the constraint, why does it exist, and what evidence suggests this is the right solution.


Writing Complete Funnels


Write and optimize new offer positioning, unique mechanisms, big ideas, hooks and leads, advertorials, listicles, quiz flows, long\-form and short\-form sales pages, product detail pages, offer sections, pricing and bundle presentation, guarantees, checkout copy, order bumps, post\-purchase upsells, downsells, cross\-sells, funnel transitions, calls to action, and the supporting briefs for page graphics and visual proof. You must be able to develop a major long\-form funnel from a blank page and equally to identify and rewrite the one critical section inside an existing funnel.


The Offer, Not Only the Words


Copy cannot be separated from the offer. You will think critically about positioning, price, quantity, bundles, discounts, bonuses, guarantees, payment options, shipping thresholds, subscription structures, order bumps, upsell sequencing and offer continuity through the funnel. You should be willing to conclude that the copy is not the main problem and that the right recommendation is to change the offer, reorder the upsells, change the price, improve the guarantee, remove a step or target a different segment. Your responsibility is to improve the commercial result, not to defend the original brief.


Funnel Economics


Understand the underlying economics of each offer, including selling price, cost of goods, pick and pack, shipping, payment processing, discounts, refunds, chargebacks, subscription take rates, upsell margins, gross and contribution margin, customer acquisition cost, and revenue and profit per visitor. A higher AOV is not automatically better if contribution margin falls, a higher conversion rate is not better if refunds rise, and a pricing test must be judged on full funnel economics rather than one isolated metric. You do not need to be a finance professional. You do need to think like an owner.


Staying Close to Live Performance


Once your copy is launched, confirm the correct version went live, review performance against the control and at each funnel step, segment where appropriate, compare mobile and desktop, look for discrepancies between traffic sources, use heatmaps and behavioural data where helpful, and compare primary against guardrail metrics. Document what worked, what did not and why, recommend the next action, and feed every meaningful learning back into research and writing. You should feel personal ownership of the result without becoming defensive when an idea loses. A losing test that produces a real learning is useful. A test launched without a hypothesis and never reviewed is not.


The Learning System and AI Leverage


Build and maintain a searchable archive of tests and results recording the original problem, hypothesis, change, result and learning. Identify recurring patterns across brands and funnel types, separate genuine principles from conclusions drawn on insufficient data, convert repeated winners into reusable frameworks, and prevent failed concepts from being unknowingly repeated. Insight should become company knowledge rather than living in one person's head.


Alongside that, become highly AI\-enabled. Use and improve AI\-assisted systems for research synthesis, voice\-of\-customer clustering, transcript and review analysis, competitor and mechanism research, angle development, hypothesis generation, copy outlining, first drafts, variations, objection identification, quality control, claim consistency review, funnel analysis and test documentation. You will not use a generic chatbot to produce first drafts. You will help build structured processes containing the right context, approved source material, brand knowledge, customer research, historical winners, founder frameworks, defined quality criteria and clear review stages. The standard is not whether AI was used. It is whether AI helped us produce better research, better copy, more tests and faster learning without lowering quality.


What We Are Looking For


Substantial professional experience in direct response copywriting, gained over several years writing for real offers with meaningful traffic. A portfolio containing both long\-form and short\-form funnel copy, significant experience writing for cold traffic, and proven experience in DTC ecommerce, direct response or another measurable\-response environment. Evidence that your work has generated meaningful revenue or measurable conversion improvement. Experience writing complete funnels rather than isolated page sections, including advertorials, listicles, sales pages, quizzes, checkouts and post\-purchase upsells.


Experience in health, wellness, supplements or another claims\-sensitive category, and an understanding of how to build belief where the benefit is not visually demonstrable. A strong grasp of customer awareness, market sophistication, offers, mechanisms, leads, proof, objections and risk reversal. The ability to conduct and synthesize deep customer research and turn it into a clear hypothesis and a persuasive argument.


Strong analytical fluency and comfort with funnel performance data, the ability to diagnose where a funnel is losing customers, a working understanding of AOV, revenue per visitor, upsell take rates, gross margin and contribution margin, experience creating and evaluating conversion tests, and the ability to distinguish correlation, noise and meaningful evidence.


Strong AI fluency with evidence of using AI inside a real research, writing or analysis workflow. The ability to write quickly without sacrificing strategic depth, the confidence to challenge a weak brief or assumption, the humility to change direction when the data disproves an idea, the communication skills to work with founders, media buyers, designers and analysts, and the potential to train and lead additional writers as the function grows. You must be able to overlap consistently with our collaboration window of 8:00am to 12:00pm EST.


High\-volume Meta, native, Google or affiliate traffic, post\-purchase upsell funnels, portfolio or multi\-brand environments, CRO or direct response agencies, subscription offers, and experience building copy systems or training programs are all highly advantageous.


Evidence We Expect to See


Applicants should demonstrate results, not simply submit polished writing samples. Strong evidence includes funnel revenue, conversion rate improvements, revenue per visitor and AOV improvements, upsell take rate and contribution margin improvements, results against an established control, evidence of scaling an offer, before and after funnel performance, and a sequence of tests showing how an insight developed over time.


We understand that candidates may be under confidentiality agreements. Results can be anonymized, but you should still be able to explain what the offer was, what the original problem was, what you personally owned, what research you conducted, what hypothesis you formed, what you changed, which metric moved, how much traffic supported the conclusion, and what happened next. We are more interested in clear thinking and honest attribution than impressive numbers without context.


This Role Is Not


This is not a junior copywriting position, a brand copy role, a content or social media role, or an ad\-copy\-only position. It is not a role where you write from a brief without questioning it, where your responsibility ends when the document is submitted, or where you would rather your work was not measured. It is not a pure CRO analyst role in which you never write, nor a management\-only role in which you no longer produce. It is not for someone who uses AI to generate generic copy and calls that leverage, who needs the founders to supply every angle and mechanism, who waits to be told which test to run, or who blames media buying, design or development without investigating the full funnel.

 **Benefits**  

What We Offer


A fully remote senior position with genuine ownership of a function that directly determines how fast the business can move. We offer paid time off, a monthly wellness stipend, medical insurance support, a company\-funded computer allowance after a tenure milestone, a birthday gift card, an in\-country meetup allowance, and participation in company\-funded leadership offsites. You will have direct access to the founders, a high\-volume testing environment, and the mandate to build the system rather than inherit someone else's process.

description:
**About the Role**
------------------



Xsolla is looking for a Senior Delivery Manager to help bring greater clarity, coordination, and operational discipline across our product development teams.



This role sits at the center of product execution, working closely with Product Managers, Engineers, Designers, Analytics, Marketing, and other Delivery Managers to ensure teams are aligned on priorities, dependencies, timelines, and changes.



The Senior Delivery Manager will own the operating rhythm of the team: maintaining the backlog and roadmap, running engineering ceremonies, surfacing risks and blockers, and ensuring that changes are communicated clearly—not just what is changing, but why.



Beyond day\-to\-day delivery, this person will also play an important role in identifying broader operational challenges and working with leadership to improve how the team plans, communicates, prioritizes, and executes.



### **Key Responsibilities**


### **Cross\-Functional Alignment**


* Work closely with Product Managers, Engineers, Designers, Analytics, Marketing, Project Managers, and other stakeholders to ensure alignment across initiatives.
* Maintain visibility into dependencies, timelines, priorities, and risks across teams.
* Proactively identify areas where teams are becoming misaligned and drive the conversations necessary to resolve them.
* Ensure stakeholders understand both what the team is doing and how individual activities connect to broader product and business priorities.

### **Team Execution \& Scrum**


* Run and facilitate engineering scrum ceremonies, including stand\-ups, sprint planning, refinement, retrospectives, and other working sessions as needed.
* Ensure teams leave meetings with clear decisions, owners, and next steps.
* Track blockers and risks through resolution rather than simply documenting them.
* Help create a predictable and effective operating cadence between Product and Engineering.

### **Backlog \& Roadmap Management**


* Build, maintain, and continuously improve the team backlog and roadmap in partnership with Product and Engineering leadership.
* Ensure work is clearly prioritized, appropriately structured, and visible to stakeholders.
* Maintain clarity between committed roadmap work, future opportunities, operational improvements, and unscheduled backlog items.
* Identify dependencies, sequencing challenges, and resource conflicts before they become delivery issues.

### **Change Management \& Communication**


* Communicate changes to priorities, timelines, scope, and direction clearly and proactively.
* Help teams understand the why behind changes so that Engineers, Designers, and other stakeholders have the context necessary to make better decisions.
* Ensure important decisions and changes are documented and communicated consistently across impacted teams.
* Help reduce confusion caused by fragmented or inconsistent communication.

### **Operational Improvement**


* Identify recurring execution challenges, process breakdowns, organizational friction, and operational gaps.
* Work with leadership to understand root causes and define strategies for addressing them.
* Translate operational strategies into actionable improvements for the team.
* Continuously evaluate how planning, prioritization, communication, and execution processes can be improved.
* Encourage accountability across teams and help ensure problems are driven toward resolution rather than passed between functions.
### **What Success Looks Like**



Success in this role means teams have greater clarity and predictability in how they operate.



The right candidate will help create an environment where:


* Teams understand what the highest priorities are and why.
* Product, Engineering, Design, Analytics, and Marketing remain aligned as plans evolve.
* Roadmaps and backlogs accurately reflect the work of the team.
* Risks and dependencies are surfaced early rather than discovered late.
* Changes are communicated clearly and with appropriate context.
* Meetings result in decisions and action rather than additional ambiguity.
* Operational problems are identified proactively and systematically improved.
* Leadership has confidence in the team’s ability to execute against its commitments.
### **Skills \& Experience**


### **Strong Communication**


* Exceptional written and verbal communication skills.
* Able to communicate effectively across technical, product, creative, and business teams.
* Comfortable facilitating discussions involving competing priorities or viewpoints.

title: Senior Technical Director, Release Management & Automation (AI)
Head of Web Production (DTC Growth Technology) Digital Production Director
description:
About Us


HarZa Group is a fast\-growing operator of direct\-to\-consumer brands in health and wellness. Our flagship brand, Rejuvacare, serves more than 400,000 customers with products targeting chronic pain and mobility, including RejuvaKnee, FootRenew, RejuvaFlow and OzemPatch. We ship primarily to the United States and run a membership program that powers recurring revenue. The company has scaled 12x in a single year to nearly 150 people across more than 15 countries. We are remote\-first, async\-first, and hold a high standard of accountability across everything we do.


The Role


We are a direct\-to\-consumer business where technology is a direct function of marketing. Our marketing team can develop a campaign idea and write the copy for it in a single day, but that idea only starts producing revenue once it has become a live, accurate and fully functioning landing page, checkout or funnel. The speed of our production function therefore sets the speed of the entire business.


We are hiring a Head of Web Production to build and own the operating system through which marketing requirements become live digital experiences. Your responsibility is not to manage tasks, chase deadlines or add project management meetings. It is to redesign how the work gets done. You will examine every stage of production, remove unnecessary handoffs, improve requirements, manage dependencies, install effective quality controls, and decide where AI, automation, page builders, reusable components or traditional development should be used.


For every requirement you should be asking whether this genuinely needs a developer, whether it can be built from an existing component or template, whether an AI\-enabled page builder can complete most of it, whether the marketing team can safely complete it without engineering, whether the requirement can be eliminated or standardized, whether the quality check can be automated, and why it is taking as long as it is. Your job is to protect the business objective while continuously challenging the method used to achieve it.


To be explicit about scope, this is not a cloud infrastructure or site reliability role. This is web production and development operations for a high\-volume direct response marketing business.

 **Requirements**  

What You Will Own


The Production Operating System


Map and redesign the workflow from marketing request to production launch, identifying bottlenecks, unnecessary handoffs, waiting time and duplicated work, and establishing clear ownership at every stage. Define what information must exist before work can begin, create work\-in\-progress limits and prioritization rules, and build separate production lanes for urgent changes, standard pages, experiments and complex technical projects so that urgent work stops destroying the predictability of planned work. Create clear escalation paths for blockers and for requirements that change mid\-build.


Requirements and Task Definition


Build standardized briefs for landing pages, checkouts, funnels, upsells and technical changes, and establish a Definition of Ready for every category of work so that incomplete or ambiguous requests never enter development. Ensure every requirement carries complete copy, design direction, references, responsive behaviour, tracking requirements and acceptance criteria, and translate marketing intent into specifications that developers and page builders can execute without repeated clarification. Create a controlled process for requirements that change after development has begun.


AI\-First Production


Audit the full production process for opportunities to use AI and automation, evaluate AI coding tools, AI page builders, no\-code platforms, reusable components and template\-based systems, and determine the right balance between developers, page builders, designers and AI\-enabled operators. Build workflows where AI converts approved briefs, copy and designs into high\-quality first drafts, install guardrails that allow non\-developers to build safely without damaging performance, tracking or brand standards, and reduce repetitive development through reusable sections and approved design systems. Measure the actual impact of AI on cycle time, cost, quality and throughput rather than assuming it.


Dependencies and Capacity


Create visibility over the workload and capacity of development, design and other shared resources, identify dependencies before work enters production, and sequence work based on when copy, graphics, video, development and approvals will realistically be available. Prevent developers from being assigned work that cannot be completed because a dependency is missing, build a capacity planning system that lets marketing understand what can actually be delivered and when, and surface constraints early enough for the business to reprioritize or find an alternative. Reduce reliance on informal messages and on individual managers holding critical information in their heads.


Quality Built Into the Process


Move quality control upstream instead of relying on final\-stage inspection. Introduce developer self\-QC before any task is submitted, create standardized QC checklists by page and funnel type, define acceptance criteria before development begins, and establish an independent final QC process that does not depend entirely on one person. Implement automated testing wherever practical, including visual regression, broken links, responsive layouts, tracking, checkout functionality, browser compatibility and page performance. Categorize defects, track root causes, and ensure repeated defects change the underlying system, checklist, component or training rather than being corrected one at a time.


Team Structure and Capability


Lead the existing production team and raise its operating standard. Determine which work should be completed by developers and which should be completed by AI\-enabled production specialists, and make sure capability is matched to the work. Coach the team on estimation, task clarification, self\-QC and AI\-assisted workflows, set clear performance expectations for speed, predictability and quality, and build enough documentation and shared visibility that the function does not depend on any single person holding critical context.


The Measurement System


Build and maintain reporting on request\-to\-launch cycle time, active production time versus waiting time, throughput by work category, on\-time delivery, clarification interactions after assignment, first\-pass QC rate, average revision rounds, escaped defect rate, rework hours, blocker age, the share of work completed through reusable components or AI\-assisted workflows, cost per page or funnel, and marketing launch delays caused by technology or creative dependencies. These metrics exist to improve the system, not to generate reporting.


How Success Will Be Measured


Your first thirty days are about establishing a baseline. We do not currently measure cycle time, waiting time, clarification loops, rework or escaped defects, so your first task is to map the current state from request to launch and put real numbers against it, then produce a prioritized roadmap for improving the system. We would rather agree ambitious targets against real data than hand you numbers invented before anyone measured anything.


By sixty days we expect a standardized intake and requirements process, clear Definitions of Ready and Done, service\-level expectations by category of work, visibility over development and creative capacity, dependency planning across copy, design, video, development, tracking and approvals, piloted AI\-assisted and template\-driven workflows, and a live operating dashboard covering speed, quality and throughput.


By ninety days we expect the function to be trending strongly toward a materially shorter median request\-to\-launch cycle time, the large majority of work delivered by the committed date, the large majority of work passing final QC without another development round, a sharp reduction in issues identified after approval by the CEO or the media buyer, full visibility over active work, dependencies, blockers and capacity, standard page types produced without bespoke development, and higher throughput without a corresponding increase in headcount. Exact targets will be finalized against your baseline.  

  

What We Are Looking For


Significant experience improving the operations of a web development, digital production or growth technology team, with a proven record of reducing delivery time, increasing throughput or improving first\-pass quality. Experience in an environment where development speed directly affects revenue. A strong working understanding of landing pages, ecommerce funnels, checkouts, upsells, testing and conversion\-focused web production.


Enough technical depth to challenge estimates, architecture choices and development approaches, including a working understanding of HTML, CSS, JavaScript, APIs, analytics, tracking, page builders and modern web development workflows. Experience implementing AI tools or automation inside a real production environment rather than as a pilot or a talking point. Experience designing intake processes, acceptance criteria, capacity planning and quality control systems, and a strong grasp of dependencies and constraint management.


The ability to communicate effectively with marketers, copywriters, designers, media buyers and developers, and the confidence to challenge senior stakeholders when a requirement is unclear, unnecessarily complicated or being solved in the wrong way. Strong analytical ability, comfort making decisions from operational data, and a bias toward simplification, standardization and measurable results.


Experience with direct response ecommerce, high\-volume web production, Shopify, Checkout Champ, Figma, landing page builders, CRO testing and marketing analytics is highly advantageous. Formal qualifications are not required where there is strong evidence of relevant outcomes. You must be able to overlap consistently with our collaboration window of 8:00am to 12:00pm EST.


This Role Is Not


This is not a traditional cloud\-infrastructure DevOps role, a Jira administration role, a project coordinator position, or a role focused on running agile ceremonies. It is not a role for someone who accepts every requirement without questioning it, whose first answer to any constraint is additional headcount, who can describe AI tools but has never embedded them into an operational workflow, or who wants engineering leadership disconnected from marketing and revenue.

 **Benefits**  

What We Offer


A fully remote senior position with genuine ownership of a function that directly determines how fast the business can move. We offer paid time off, a monthly wellness stipend, medical insurance support, a company\-funded computer allowance after a tenure milestone, a birthday gift card, an in\-country meetup allowance, and participation in company\-funded leadership offsites. You will have direct access to the founders, a high\-volume testing environment, and the mandate to build the system rather than inherit someone else's process.

title: AI Product Ops & AI Enablement Lead
description:
**Company Description**  

NIQ is standing up a new PM Operations \& AI Enablement group: a small, build\-weighted internal product team that creates AI\-powered tools for our product organization and drives the adoption that makes them land. We are looking for the Lead Product Manager who will own that portfolio end to end.


This is a product management role, not a coordination role. You will carry a portfolio of internal products with real users, a measured quality bar, adoption targets and sunset decisions — and you will own the operating practices that make our product teams faster and better evidenced. Think of it as being the product manager for the product managers.


You will lead a cross\-functional group of engineers without direct reporting lines, which means you will deliver through shared goals, written agreements and visible artifacts rather than instruction. We are explicit about this because it shapes who succeeds here.


The two pilots are an AI toolchain for the software development lifecycle, and our design system.

 **Job Description**  

Strategy and portfolio


– The group’s product vision, direction and strategy for a 12–18 month roadmap: what gets built, in what order, and why.


– Portfolio prioritization and capacity allocation, including how many tools the group can responsibly carry at once.


– The build\-versus\-buy recommendation for every initiative, against a buy\-or\-configure\-first default, and the business case behind it.


– The sunset decision for tools that do not earn their adoption.


– A two\-to\-three year view of how AI changes product and engineering work, and a roadmap that stays consistent with it.


Building AI products


– End\-to\-end product definition for the group’s AI tooling: problem, users, the workflow it replaces, the adoption path, the measurement plan, the maintenance owner.


– AI\-native specifications a strong engineer can build from — task boundaries, context sources, failure modes, guardrails, human\-in\-the\-loop points, and the quality bar in numbers.


– The product calls that shape the architecture: workflow versus agent, retrieval versus fine\-tuning, model selection per use case, and the cost and latency budget.


– The quality bar and evaluation strategy: what "good enough" means before the build starts, a failure taxonomy built from real usage, and the regression discipline when prompts or models change.


– How the human enters the loop, how uncertainty is shown, and what happens when the system does not know — the decisions that determine whether people trust the tool.


– The incident and rollback plan for non\-deterministic failure, written before launch.

  

Adoption


– The adoption outcome, measured as instrumented depth of use — not seats provisioned or enthusiasm in a demo.


– The adoption path for each tool: pilot teams, a champion in each team, onboarding, office hours, handover to support.


– Evangelizing the work across product and engineering: the demo, the prototype, the case made repeatedly and well.


– Facilitating the sessions where practice actually changes and leaving them with commitments rather than sentiment.


– Change management, rollout, training and enablement content.


– Honest reconciliation of instrumented usage against self\-reported benefit, and ownership of the gap.


Practice and craft


– The product operating standards for the organization — intake, prioritization inputs, PRD conventions, definition of done, documentation, decision log — kept deliberately light.


– Coaching and mentoring product managers, particularly those earlier in their careers, in continuous discovery, outcome framing, evidence\-based decision\-making and AI\-native practice.


– The AI literacy curriculum for the product organization — designed and taught or outsourced.


– Recurring forums where teams share what they discovered and what they decided.


Measurement and reporting


– The definition, baseline and instrumentation for the programme’s success metrics, quantitative and qualitative.


– A metric\-led reporting cadence to senior leadership, including the results that did not work.


– The trade\-off framework — speed, reliability, cost, data risk — communicated in writing.


Governance partnership


– The product\-side data decisions: what data each surface accepts, which model serves which use case, and the guardrails that go with it.


– Partnership with Legal, Privacy, Security and IT on data classification, model approval, access and responsible\-AI standards.

 **Qualifications**  

Required


– Senior product leadership experience in enterprise B2B SaaS, with end\-to\-end ownership from discovery through delivery, and the ability to show what changed as a result.


– Experience leading and growing cross\-functional teams, and mentoring product and design practitioners.


– Demonstrated ability to deliver through people who do not report to you — with concrete examples of aligning stakeholders who had different priorities, and of moving an organization to a new way of working that stuck.


– Hands\-on experience designing and shipping generative or agentic AI capabilities in a live product — not only using AI tools to accelerate your own work.


– Working fluency in AI product practice: prompt and context design, retrieval, agentic workflow patterns, guardrails, human\-in\-the\-loop design, and model evaluation. You can discuss model trade\-offs, data requirements, cost and latency with engineers without needing first\-principles explanations.


– Experience defining what "good enough" means for an AI feature in measurable terms, and holding a product to it. – Experience creating or scaling a design system and driving its adoption across teams.


– Strong research and evidence practice: usability testing, interviews, journey mapping, surveys, A/B testing — run to a professional standard and taught to others.


– Strong customer research and evidence practice: conducting interviews and gathering insights for creating informed decisions.


– Product analytics fluency (for example Amplitude, Pendo, Tableau) and the quantitative literacy to define a metric that survives scrutiny.


– Experience defining and embedding operating practice — design ops, product ops, intake, process and documentation standards — that teams adopted willingly.


– Facilitation skills with senior and skeptical audiences, and experience designing and delivering enablement or training programmes.


– Commercial judgement: business\-case creation, budget ownership, and vendor or partner evaluation.


– Excellent written communication: you make your case in a document that survives the meeting you were not in.


– Fluent English


Preferred


– Formal grounding in AI product development


– Experience with agentic development tooling in your own workflow, and a view on what it changes about how teams work.


– Familiarity with engineering productivity measurement (DORA, SPACE, DX Core 4\) and clear views on what each does and does not measure.

– Working knowledge of AI governance obligations in the EU and beyond, including AI literacy requirements for internal AI use.
